host: Intel Core Ultra 7 270K Plus, Linux x86_64, 24 logical CPUs, shared

commands.rebuild: perf stat --no-scale -e instructions:u,task-clock -x, -o <sample>.perf cargo build --locked -p moq-mux --lib --timings

limitations: Shared host; one cold observation per profile. Unit durations overlap and are not CPU attribution.
Release measurement uses default features, not the shipping OpenH264 FFI build.
MBX_DISABLE is only for the controlled compilation measurements; mbx_incremental runs through mbx.
No production patch is retained; incomplete candidate release rebuilds were stopped and excluded.

reader_candidate.conclusion: Library IR falls by 10 lines, test IR grows by 904, and rebuild CPU and instructions do not improve beyond noise.

shipping_lto.command: CARGO_TARGET_DIR=<fresh target per profile> cargo build-ffi --release --timings

superseded.reason: The first comparison built fat into a target the default-feature release build had already filled, so 300 of its 474 units were fresh and timed at 0 s; thin's profile change rebuilt them (202.16 s). Its whole-command totals compared unequal work and are replaced by the cold rerun above.

runtime_method.build: cargo bench --locked -p moq-net --features fuzz --bench session --no-run (fat and thin release profiles)

shipping_lto.decision: Keep fat LTO for now, the maintainer's 2026-10-20 choice. From equally cold targets, thin cut whole-command wall by 12.5% at about equal CPU (+1.7%) and grew the archive by 14.5%; runtime evidence is noisy. Switching is left as an open maintainer decision.

mbx_incremental.edit: append one comment line to rs/moq-net/src/lib.rs; edits 1 to 3 accumulate, restore reverts the file

variants.mbx: the normal mbx Cargo shim, its shared cache and learned incremental state
variants.plain: MBX_DISABLE=1 CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 in a private target directory
